title: Photon-Statistics Control of Strong-Field Rydberg-State Excitation
authors: Tao Jiang, Jinlei Liu, Haopu Dou, Lingyi Zhao, Peng Xiang, Liangjun Peng, Renyu Wang, Jing Zhao, Xiaowei Wang, Yue Lang, Zengxiu Zhao
abstract: Photon statistics provides a new control dimension for strong-field bound-state formation. Using a quantum-optical phase-space formulation coupled to time-dependent Schrödinger-equation calculations, we show that field fluctuations enhance multiphoton Rydberg excitation by broadening AC-Stark-shifted resonances, but suppress tunneling-mediated recapture even as ionization increases. A quantum-statistical recapture model attributes the latter to ensemble-induced dispersion of relative path phases. Photon statistics also reshapes Rydberg-manifold parity, linking field statistics to recapture coherence and final-state symmetry.
summary: This paper demonstrates that photon statistics provide a new control knob for strong-field atomic physics, specifically controlling Rydberg-state excitation. Using advanced quantum-optical models, the authors show that field fluctuations enhance excitation in the multiphoton regime but suppress it in the tunneling regime. This highlights that field statistics can independently control both the probability and the symmetry of the final bound electronic state.
main_problem: The study investigates how the statistical properties of the driving laser field (photon statistics) can be used as a novel control mechanism to govern the formation of bound states, specifically Rydberg-state excitation (RSE), in strong-field atomic interactions.
main_result: Field fluctuations enhance multiphoton RSE by broadening resonance access, but they suppress the RSE mediated by tunneling, a suppression attributed to the ensemble-induced dispersion of relative path phases.
method: The research employs a combination of a quantum-optical phase-space formulation coupled to time-dependent Schrödinger equation (TDSE) calculations and a Quantum-Statistical Recapture (QSR) model.
model_or_system: The system models an atom (like Hydrogen) interacting with intense quantum light fields, comparing coherent, Bright Squeezed Vacuum (BSV), and Phase-Squeezed Coherent (PSC) states. The dynamics are governed by the joint atom-field density operator.
key_observables: Rydberg-state excitation (RSE) yield, Rydberg-manifold parity, and the decomposition of RSE into individual-path and interference components.
important_parameters: Photon statistics (field fluctuations), mean peak intensity, and the distinction between the multiphoton and tunneling ionization regimes.
main_assumptions: The analysis utilizes the electric-dipole approximation and relies on the QSR model, which treats the field statistics via ensemble averaging.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate RSE dynamics comparing coherent vs. BSV driving, showing yield dependence on intensity, and demonstrating how photon statistics reshape the parity composition of the final Rydberg manifold.
paper_structure: The paper systematically compares the effects of different field statistics (coherent vs. squeezed) on RSE across different intensity regimes, using the QSR model to quantify the enhancement in the multiphoton regime and the suppression in the tunneling regime.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses how nonclassical light properties (photon statistics) can be harnessed to control quantum dynamics, offering a powerful tool for manipulating final-state symmetries and excitation probabilities in atomic physics.

FIG. 4. Photon-statistical imprint on the parity composition of the final Rydberg manifold. (a), (b) Normalized orbital- angular-momentum distributions of the Rydberg population for coherent driving and PSC driving with χ = 10−3, respec- tively. (c) Rydberg-manifold parity PR(I) as a function of the mean peak intensity for coherent, PSC, and BSV driv- ing. Positive (negative) values of PR indicate predominantly even- (odd-) parity excitation, whereas PR ≃0 corresponds to a parity-mixed manifold. Increasing field fluctuations drive the strongly parity-selective coherent-field response toward a parity-mixed final-state distribution.
